result: Kept, confirmed in its own failures. The camera's four rules each play as a take: the dailies show the lens in the ram's wool and the night wide almost black (take one of the Rams, 88b35af3), the cinematographer states each new rule in his close; Polyphemus gets his close from below, the underside of his jaw and the eye up at the top of the frame, half in shadow ('That is my good side.'); the stone take one cuts and the stone is in the door, take two holds on the giant bent over it and heaving it; the milking's dailies, take one and take two, are both dark behind ('Keep it.'). Weak: in several closes the back of a crew member's head fills the side of the frame (the director's 'Where is the camera?', the AD's 'Why is the camera in the ram?', the cinematographer's 'I go where the heat is'); 'Did anyone see it move?' is shot from behind the director; in take two the door is out of frame, so the stone is seen heaved, not seen arriving; the last shot holds the crew from behind.
